raw_text:
name: dotnet-csharp-source-generators

Creates and consumes Roslyn source generators in .NET: `IIncrementalGenerator`, syntax providers, semantic analysis, emission, diagnostics, `CSharpGeneratorDriver` testing, NuGet packaging, `[GeneratedRegex]`, `[LoggerMessage]`, System.Text.Json source generation, and `[JsonSerializable]`.

See [skill:dotnet-roslyn-analyzers], [skill:dotnet-csharp-modern-patterns], and [skill:dotnet-csharp-coding-standards] for related analyzers, modern C#, partial properties, and naming.

Source generators are shipped as analyzers targeting `netstandard2.0`.

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
<TargetFramework>netstandard2.0</TargetFramework>
<EnforceExtendedAnalyzerRules>true</EnforceExtendedAnalyzerRules>
<IsRoslynComponent>true</IsRoslynComponent>
<LangVersion>latest</LangVersion>
<PackageReference Include="Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Analyzers" Version="3.3.4" PrivateAssets="all" />
<PackageReference Include="Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp" Version="4.12.0" PrivateAssets="all" />
```

> **Always target `netstandard2.0`.** Generators load into the compiler process, which requires this TFM for compatibility. Use `LangVersion>latest` to write modern C# in the generator itself.

Always use `IIncrementalGenerator` over the legacy `ISourceGenerator`. Incremental generators are cache-aware and only re-run when inputs change, making them significantly faster in IDE scenarios.

```csharp
public sealed class AutoNotifyGenerator : IIncrementalGenerator
public void Initialize(IncrementalGeneratorInitializationContext context)
```

Use `ForAttributeWithMetadataName` or `CreateSyntaxProvider` with tight predicates. Transform to simple data: strings/records. Never pass `ISymbol` or `SyntaxNode` through the pipeline (they hold the compilation alive and break caching). Use `record struct` or `IEquatable<T>` for value equality. Emit deterministic output with `// <auto-generated/>` and `#nullable enable`.

Use fully qualified names, group candidates by containing type, and emit one `{TypeName}.{Feature}.g.cs` file per type. Handle global namespaces. This example targets top-level, non-generic classes; production generators must handle generic and nested types, or report a diagnostic for unsupported shapes rather than emitting invalid code.

Report errors and warnings through `SourceProductionContext` rather than throwing exceptions. Capture syntax `Location` for diagnostics. `Location` is not value-equatable; exclude it from pipeline equality or report before projecting to value types. Prefer raw string literals for templates.

Use `RegisterPostInitializationOutput` for marker attributes and helper types independent of user code.

Test with `CSharpGeneratorDriver`:
```csharp
var syntaxTree = CSharpSyntaxTree.ParseText(source);
var references = AppDomain.CurrentDomain.GetAssemblies()
.Where(a => !a.IsDynamic && !string.IsNullOrEmpty(a.Location))
.Select(a => MetadataReference.CreateFromFile(a.Location))
var compilation = CSharpCompilation.Create("TestAssembly",
new CSharpCompilationOptions(OutputKind.DynamicallyLinkedLibrary));
var generator = new AutoNotifyGenerator();
GeneratorDriver driver = CSharpGeneratorDriver.Create(generator);
driver = driver.RunGeneratorsAndUpdateCompilation(
compilation, out var outputCompilation, out var diagnostics);
Assert.Empty(diagnostics.Where(d => d.Severity == DiagnosticSeverity.Error));
var runResult = driver.GetRunResult();
Assert.Single(runResult.GeneratedTrees);
```
Use [Verify.SourceGenerators](https://github.com/VerifyTests/Verify.SourceGenerators) for snapshot tests.

GeneratedRegex: method must be `static partial` returning `Regex`, on a `partial class` or `partial struct`. It is compile-time, AOT-compatible, and replaces `new Regex(...)`; `RegexOptions.Compiled` is ignored.

LoggerMessage: methods must be `static partial` in a `partial class`; `{Placeholder}` parameters are structured data. `Exception` is logged automatically (do not include in message template). Event IDs are auto-assigned; specify explicit IDs for stable telemetry.

System.Text.Json source generation is AOT-compatible and avoids reflection. Register every type with `[JsonSerializable]`; use `TypeInfoResolverChain` (net8.0+) to combine contexts. Required for Native AOT -- reflection-based serialization is trimmed. Use `[JsonDerivedType]` for polymorphism.

```xml
<ProjectReference Include="..\MyGenerator\MyGenerator.csproj"
```

NuGet generators go under `analyzers/dotnet/cs/`:
```xml
<IncludeBuildOutput>false</IncludeBuildOutput>
<DevelopmentDependency>true</DevelopmentDependency>
<None Include="$(OutputPath)\$(AssemblyName).dll"
PackagePath="analyzers/dotnet/cs" />
```
Include `_._` if no runtime dependency. For debugger attachment:
```csharp
if (!System.Diagnostics.Debugger.IsAttached)
System.Diagnostics.Debugger.Launch();
```
For generated files:
```xml
<EmitCompilerGeneratedFiles>true</EmitCompilerGeneratedFiles>
<CompilerGeneratedFilesOutputPath>Generated</CompilerGeneratedFilesOutputPath>
```
Add `Generated/` to `.gitignore`.

References: [Source Generator Cookbook](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/main/docs/features/incremental-generators.cookbook.md), [Incremental Generators](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/main/docs/features/incremental-generators.md), [GeneratedRegex source generator](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/base-types/regular-expression-source-generators), [Compile-time logging source generation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/extensions/logger-message-generator), [System.Text.Json source generation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/serialization/system-text-json/source-generation), [ .NET Framework Design Guidelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/design-guidelines/).
